items.title: Muggsy Spanier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: I liked Freddie very much. He didn't make many records. ... I heard it was a place on 35th Street, I think 35th and Prairie. Jimmy Noon was in the band. There was a four-piece band and Teddy Weatherford was playing the piano. Oh, yeah. And I think Tubby Hall was playing the drums.

ctx.x: You wouldn't know it because you recorded so much and it sounds great. I remember Rod Kless, your old clarinetist on that Bluebird band that you had, the Ragtime band, told me once he studied a little bit, actually took a couple lessons from Dodds, I think. He used to go down and actually practically study with him, if not actual formal lessons, at least get ideas from him to his home, I think, to study.

Well, we all used to go down on the Southside and listen to all those bands. Chicago at that time was just full of good bands. It was in a place you could go that you wouldn't hear a good band. You had Freddie Kepler, Jimmy Noon. That's when Zutty was in his prime. And Sid Catler was just coming up then. Yeah.
Well, how was Freddie Kepler? Did you ever listen to him much? Oh, yes.
